title: the Lalita Sahasranama (selections)
hook: a woman who is Mom at breakfast and Doctor by nine, and a hymn of names that begins with Mother before it says Queen

segments.voice: Yesterday, the last of the Sri Sukta days: the hymn asked Kardama, the mud, to bring the lotus mother home. Whose unglamorous part did you thank? Today, a new hymn, made of names. Day one thousand one hundred.
screen: `THE SRI SUKTA.` · `THE LOTUS ASKS THROUGH THE MUD.`

segments.voice: At seven in the morning she's Mom, hunting for a missing shoe. By nine she's Doctor, signing charts. At lunch a friend calls her by a nickname from college. At the temple an old aunty calls her beta, child. Same woman. Every name catches a different side of her, and nobody who loves her would pick just one. Now take that and make it vast. The Lalita Sahasranama is a hymn made almost entirely of names for the goddess, one after another, line after line. Today, how it opens, and the first words it reaches for.
screen: `MOM AT SEVEN. DOCTOR BY NINE.` → `EVERY NAME, A DIFFERENT SIDE.` → `A HYMN MADE OF NAMES.`

segments.voice: Sahasranama means a thousand names, and Lalita is the goddess they belong to. Tradition places the hymn in the Brahmanda Purana, as a teaching the god Hayagriva gives to the sage Agastya. Some who worship her recite it name by name, at home or in temples. A hymn of names works differently from a story. There's no plot. Each name is a small window, and you look through one, then the next. Over the coming days the path will open a few of those windows, not all of them. So, the first three names. In paraphrase. Sri Mata: the auspicious Mother. Sri Maharajni: the great Queen. Srimat Simhasaneshvari: she who rules from the glorious lion throne. Notice the order. Mother first. Before the crown, before the throne, before any of her power is named, the hymn calls her Mother. Some teachers say that's the key to the whole hymn: whatever she is later, a warrior, a queen, the power behind the universe, she is that as a mother, and the one reciting comes to her as a child. Then the throne, and the lion. Royal names, and the lion carries an echo of the fierce goddess the path met in the Devi Mahatmya. And notice the first sound. Sri. The same word the Sri Sukta days were built on, radiance and fortune, the goddess of the lotus. Here it's the opening breath of the very first name. Some readers hear the two hymns meeting there: the fortune of the Sri Sukta becomes the Mother of the thousand names. Others simply hear an auspicious first word, a good way to begin.
screen: `A HYMN MADE OF NAMES.` · `SRI MATA, THE MOTHER.` · `GREAT QUEEN, ON THE LION THRONE.` · `THE FIRST SOUND IS SRI.` · then, large: `MOTHER BEFORE QUEEN.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: your names. Settle, and let the breath slow. Quietly list the names you're called by different people: the name your family uses, the one at work, a nickname, a title, the name only one person ever uses. Let each one come up on a breath, and notice what side of you it holds. Then notice which one feels closest to home. Rest there. If you pray, you can say the name you use for God, or for the goddess, and simply rest in it. If you don't, let your own names be enough to sit with. The bell holds the time.
The Lalita Sahasranama. A hymn of names for the goddess Lalita, which opens Sri Mata, the Mother, before Queen or throne.
Your line: the Lalita Sahasranama, selections. Today, call someone by the name they love best, the one that feels like home to them. Day one thousand one hundred.

howItsDone: Some Hindus, especially in Shakta and Sri Vidya communities, recite the Lalita Sahasranama in full at home or in temples, sometimes offering a flower or a pinch of kumkum with each name.

fork.reveal: the Lalita Sahasranama opens Sri Mata, the auspicious Mother; Queen and the lion throne come next.

original.note: Sanskrit: śrīmātā, 'the auspicious Mother,' the first name in the Lalita Sahasranama.

trapdoor: what you thought: a thousand names would be a list to get through.

what a scholar hears: śrīmātā śrīmahārājñī śrīmatsiṃhāsaneśvarī: the hymn opens with three names that each begin with śrī.

sources.ref: Lalita Sahasranama, names 1–3 (Brahmanda Purana, Lalitopakhyana, as traditionally placed)

notes: Names 1–3 paraphrased: śrīmātā, śrīmahārājñī, śrīmatsiṃhāsaneśvarī. Confirm glosses.

'Sahasranama means a thousand names' is the title's meaning; the count is not otherwise asserted. Tradition places the hymn in the Brahmanda Purana as Hayagriva's teaching to Agastya; attributed to tradition. Confirm.
'The lion carries an echo of the fierce goddess the path met in the Devi Mahatmya' is an interpretive link (Durga's lion), offered lightly; confirm or cut.
'Some teachers say that's the key to the whole hymn' (Mother before Queen) is interpretive; confirm it is fair to the commentarial tradition (e.g., Bhaskararaya).
howItsDone mentions Shakta and Sri Vidya communities and kumkum offerings with each name (kumkumarchana); confirm wording.
The meaning of the name Lalita ('she who plays', 'the lovely one') is not given aloud.

Editor pass: 'the path has spent a week with' Sri was wrong (the Sri Sukta ran ten days, 1090–1099), so the teach and the myth now say 'the Sri Sukta days'; 'in homes and temples devoted to her, people recite it, some from memory' softened to 'some who worship her recite it name by name'.
